description: One building on a labor camp: a cabin, a bath house, a kitchen, a house. What it is, how big, how many people it holds, what condition it is in, and whether it currently satisfies the three regimes that govern employer-provided farm housing — IRS Section 119, Oregon's ORS 653 wage rules, and the FSMA Produce Safety Rule's worker facility requirements.

fields.description: What is painted on the door: 'MC-Cabin-01', 'GC-BathHouse'. The docname is built from this and the parcel's abbreviation, so every camp may number its cabins from one.
fields.label: Unit Name

fields.description: What kind of building it is. A Toilet-Shower or Kitchen has no capacity and takes no assignment; a Multi-Unit Building is the barracks case where several people share one unit by design.
fields.label: Unit Type
fields.options:
Cabin
Toilet-Shower
Kitchen
Single-Family House
Multi-Unit Building
Manufactured Home
Bath House
Barn
Shop

fields.description: The parcel the building stands on.
fields.label: Parcel

fields.description: Floor area. Drives the occupancy limit under Oregon's agricultural labor housing rules, which is why an unmeasured cabin is a cabin nobody can lawfully fill.
fields.label: Square Footage

fields.description: How many people this unit sleeps, as the operation actually uses it. Compare against max_occupants_per_or_law, which is what the code allows — the two are different questions and are meant to be visible together.
fields.label: Capacity (people)

fields.description: Uninhabitable is a real answer and it is not the same as Needs Repair: one is a unit that should not be assigned, the other is a unit with a work order against it.
fields.label: Condition
fields.options:
Excellent
Good
Fair
Poor
Needs Repair
Uninhabitable

fields.description: The Fixed Asset carrying this building on the balance sheet, when there is one. Buildings depreciate; the ground under them does not, and that is the Parcel's own asset link.
fields.label: Related Asset

fields.description: The access-control zone this unit's door belongs to, for a card system that has not been installed yet. Recorded now because retrofitting zone names onto fifty doors after the fact is the expensive way to do it.
fields.label: Access Card Zone

fields.description: Where the building actually stands. A camp address is a driveway off a county road and a cabin number is a number somebody painted on a door — neither of them puts an ambulance, an inspector or a crew bus at the right building. A parcel has a boundary and a unit has a point, and the point is the one that answers 'which cabin'.
fields.label: Position

fields.description: Decimal degrees, -90 to 90. Set it with update_housing_unit. Seven decimal places is about a centimetre, which is far finer than a phone will ever fix — the precision is here so a coordinate copied from a survey is not rounded on the way in.
fields.label: GPS Latitude

fields.description: Decimal degrees, -180 to 180. Negative in the western hemisphere: a Pacific Northwest camp reads about -121, and a positive number there is a coordinate in China.
fields.label: GPS Longitude

fields.description: The facts three different regimes ask about the same building. They are on the unit rather than in a compliance register because they are also the facts that decide whether anybody can be put in it tonight: an Uninhabitable unit with no smoke detector test is not a reporting problem, it is a unit that has to stay empty.
fields.label: Compliance

fields.description: Ticked when this unit is subject to the FSMA Produce Safety Rule's worker facility requirements — a kitchen, toilet or shower serving a crew that handles covered produce, or housing inside a produce contact area. Subpart L.
fields.label: FSMA Worker Facility

fields.description: Whether this unit meets Oregon's agricultural labor housing requirements. Unknown is the honest default and it is a distinct answer from No — an operator who has not looked should not be recorded as having found a violation.
fields.label: OR Housing Law Compliant

fields.description: The occupancy the floor area allows, at 50 square feet of sleeping area per person. Computed from square_footage when left blank, and left alone once set: a unit whose bunk layout or local code says otherwise keeps the number somebody worked out.
fields.label: Max Occupants per OR Law

fields.description: When somebody last walked this unit and signed off that it is fit to live in.
fields.label: Last Habitability Inspection

fields.description: Required wherever there is a fuel-burning appliance. A blank here on a cabin with a propane heater is the single most consequential empty field on this doctype.
fields.label: CO Detector Last Test

fields.description: Somebody lives here, whether or not a Housing Assignment says so. A FIRST-CLASS source of occupancy, not a fallback: tenants already in a house at takeover (Mill Creek) never come through an assignment. Occupied puts rodent bait here in the strictest tier. It can only make a place occupied; an active Housing Assignment always counts.
fields.label: Occupied

fields.description: People work here — a barn, a shop, a packing shed. Bait here is in the occupied (strictest) tier. Types listed in ERPNext MCP Settings › Rodent Bait Program count without ticking this.
fields.label: People Work Here

fields.description: Written when a rodent bait task here is completed: a placement makes it Active; a check with consumption, fresh feeding signs or carcasses keeps it Active; a check with no activity makes it Maintenance; a completed Removal and Clearance makes it Cleared. The off-season monthly check interval applies to Maintenance only.
fields.label: Rodent Bait State

fields.description: The latest completed rodent bait placement here — the start of the current round and of its knockdown window.
fields.label: Last Bait Placement
Legal Basis
fields.options:
IRS Section 119. Lodging furnished on the business premises, for the employer's convenience, and required as a condition of employment may be excluded from the employee's wages. All three tests have to hold. The Housing Assignment records are the audit trail that defends the classification: who was housed, where, and over what dates.

ORS 653 and OAR 839-015. Oregon constrains what may be deducted from wages for housing. Each Housing Assignment carries its own housing_deduction_from_wages answer, because the question is asked of the arrangement rather than of the building.

FSMA Produce Safety Rule, Subpart L. Worker housing and facilities that touch produce contact areas carry hygiene and sanitation requirements. fsma_worker_facility is what surfaces which units those are.

None of this is legal advice, and none of these flags is a determination. They record what somebody decided, and when, so that the decision can be defended or revisited.
